title: Directives
summary: Add behavior or change appearance and layout of elements.
heading: Directives

blocks.text: A directive is an instruction you attach to an element to give it extra behavior. Angular has three kinds.

layers.title: Components
layers.detail: A directive with its own template — the ones you've been building

layers.title: Attribute directives
layers.detail: Change the look or behavior of an element (e.g. ngClass, ngStyle)

layers.title: Structural directives
layers.detail: Add or remove elements, changing the layout (e.g. @if, @for)

blocks.text: ngClass adds or removes classes based on conditions. Give it an object of class: condition pairs.

blocks.label: ngClass

blocks.text: Click to toggle the class and watch the style change:

blocks.html: Status

blocks.text: ngStyle sets one or more inline styles from your data.

blocks.label: ngStyle

blocks.text: Toggle to change the inline styles live:

blocks.html: Resize me

blocks.text: For a single class or style, the plain bindings [class.active]="isActive" and [style.color]="color" are often simpler.
ngModel is an attribute directive that binds a form control both ways (Chapter 19). It comes from FormsModule.
Structural directives add or remove elements. Modern Angular uses the built-in @if, @for, and @switch blocks (Chapter 23) for this.
Older code uses the *-prefixed forms, which you'll still see around:
The * is shorthand that wraps the element in a hidden template. Prefer the new @ blocks in fresh code.
Scaffold a directive with the CLI:

blocks.label: Terminal
blocks.code:
ng generate directive highlight
# short version:
ng g d highlight

blocks.text: A custom attribute directive is a class marked with @Directive. It can react to the host element — here it sets a yellow background.

blocks.label: highlight.directive.ts

blocks.text: Use host listeners and bindings to react to events like hover or clicks.

items: Directives add behavior to elements; components are directives with a template.
Older code uses *ngIf / *ngFor — same idea, older syntax.
Write your own with @Directive and a CSS-attribute selector.
